agent_primer:
IRS.gov is the U.S. Internal Revenue Service's website — the federal tax authority's primary citizen-facing portal. It is a website, not a desktop app. The IRS is the agency that collects federal taxes, processes tax returns, issues refunds, runs audits, manages payment plans, and administers tax-advantaged accounts. The site is server-rendered, mostly form-heavy, and authenticated personalized services route through ID.me identity verification.

**Major user-facing portals.** Six destinations cover ~90% of citizen tasks:

1. **Where's My Refund?** — `https://www.irs.gov/refunds` — the most-trafficked citizen tool. Track a federal refund by entering SSN (or ITIN) + filing status (single / married-filing-jointly / married-filing-separately / head-of-household / qualifying-surviving-spouse) + exact refund amount in whole dollars. No login required. Returns one of three statuses: "Return Received", "Refund Approved", or "Refund Sent". Updates daily, usually overnight. The amended-return tracker is a separate page at `https://www.irs.gov/filing/wheres-my-amended-return`.

2. **Get Transcript** — `https://www.irs.gov/individuals/get-transcript` — request five transcript types: **Return Transcript** (line items from your filed Form 1040), **Account Transcript** (tax assessments, payments, penalties, refunds), **Record of Account** (combined Return + Account), **Wage and Income Transcript** (W-2 / 1099 / 1098 data the IRS received from third parties), **Verification of Non-filing Letter** (proof you didn't file). Two delivery channels: **online** (instant download as PDF, requires ID.me) and **by mail** (5-10 business days, requires only address-on-file matching). Tax years available: roughly the current year + 9 prior.

3. **IRS Direct Pay** — `https://www.irs.gov/payments/direct-pay` — pay a tax balance directly from a US checking or savings account. No fee. No login required. Five payment reasons: **Tax Return or Notice** (current-year balance), **Estimated Tax** (1040-ES quarterly), **Extension** (4868 payment), **Installment Agreement** (monthly payment toward an existing plan), **Amended Return** (1040-X). Schedule up to 365 days in advance. Flow: Step 1 select reason → Step 2 verify identity (name, SSN, address from a prior return) → Step 3 enter bank info + amount → Step 4 review → Step 5 confirm + receipt. Confirmation number format: `EFT-XXXXXXXXX`.

4. **Online Account** — `https://www.irs.gov/payments/online-account` — the authenticated personalized hub. Requires ID.me login. View: account balance by tax year, payment history, scheduled payments, payment plan details, IRS notices (digital copies), economic-impact-payment history, advance child-tax-credit history. Take actions: set up a payment plan, request a transcript, update communication preferences, view notices and respond to certain ones.

5. **Forms & Publications** — `https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs` — the canonical source for downloadable IRS forms and explanatory publications. Forms are PDFs, mostly fillable. URL pattern: `https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-{number}` for the about-page (instructions, links, prior years), and direct PDFs at `https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f{number}.pdf` (form) and `https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i{number}.pdf` (instructions). Major forms: 1040 (individual return), W-2 (wage statement), W-4 (employee withholding), W-9 (taxpayer ID request), 1099-NEC (nonemployee compensation), 1099-MISC (misc income), 1098-T (tuition statement), 4868 (extension request), 1040-X (amended return), Schedule C (self-employment), Schedule D (capital gains), Schedule E (rental + pass-through income).

6. **Tax Withholding Estimator** — `https://www.irs.gov/individuals/tax-withholding-estimator` — interactive multi-step calculator that recommends a W-4 update based on income, filing status, deductions, credits. Multi-page form; results page recommends specific W-4 line entries.

**Other commonly-touched areas.** Interactive Tax Assistant (`/help/ita`) is a Q&A decision-tree tool for narrow questions ("Do I qualify for the Earned Income Tax Credit?"). Tax Topics (`/taxtopics`) are short reference pages numbered 1-901+ (Topic 152 covers refund processing, Topic 304 covers extensions, Topic 856 covers foreign tax credits). Identity Protection PIN program (`/identity-theft-fraud-scams/get-an-identity-protection-pin`) issues a 6-digit annual PIN to filers who've experienced identity theft or want preemptive protection. Installment Agreement application (`/payments/online-payment-agreement-application`) sets up monthly payment plans for outstanding balances; short-term plans (≤180 days) have no setup fee, long-term plans charge a setup fee that varies by payment method. EIN application (`/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/apply-for-an-employer-identification-number-ein-online`) is the online portal for new business EINs, available weekdays 7am-10pm ET only.

**Authentication.** Most personalized services route through **ID.me**, a federal-contracted identity verification service that requires a government photo ID + selfie + sometimes a video call. The redirect goes to `id.me` (not an IRS domain). ID.me sessions persist across IRS pages within the same browser session but expire after ~30 minutes of inactivity. Online Account, Get Transcript Online, IP PIN Online, and Tax Pro Account all use ID.me. Anonymous-but-data-gated tools (Where's My Refund, Direct Pay) verify identity via SSN + filing-status + amount or SSN + name + address; no ID.me. Sessions on these tools time out at ~15 minutes.

**Page mechanics and gotchas.**

- **PDFs are the form delivery medium.** Clicking a form link triggers a PDF download (Chrome opens it in the built-in viewer by default). Filling and saving a fillable PDF requires a viewer that supports form fields (Preview.app on macOS; not all browsers preserve filled values across reloads). Submitting filled PDFs to the IRS still requires either e-file software (paid third-party) or paper mailing.
- **Captchas appear on transactional pages.** Direct Pay's Step 4 (review) and the EIN application both gate behind reCAPTCHA. If the use-skill encounters a captcha, surface to the user; do not attempt to solve.
- **Real-time form validation.** Direct Pay and Online Account flows validate on field-blur — invalid SSNs, mismatched amounts, and bank routing-number checksums fail inline before submit. The agent should expect a field-level error message under the field, not a page-level error after submit.
- **CSP and anti-bot.** IRS.gov has strict Content-Security-Policy headers and rate-limits aggressive automation (especially on the refund tracker). High-volume lookups will hit a 429-like "unusual activity" interstitial. Treat as `vendor_friendly: hostile`. Use Rosetta against your own IRS records only.
- **Sessions and tabs.** Closing the tab during a multi-step flow (Direct Pay, ITA, Withholding Estimator) loses session state. Re-entry restarts at step 1. Many flows do not support deep links to intermediate steps.
- **Accessibility.** Forms-and-publications pages are reasonably accessible (semantic HTML, ARIA labels, alt text). The transactional flows (Direct Pay, Online Account) are partially accessible — most form fields are labeled but some custom widgets (date pickers, payment-amount entry) are unlabeled. For verification of state, prefer `interpret_check` (vision) over DOM-targeted approaches.

**URL navigation is the dominant dispatch method.** Most IRS pages have stable canonical URLs. The cmd+L → type URL → enter pattern is more robust than menu-hunting through the site's left-rail navigation, which uses a multi-level tree that varies between sections. Form pages are fully URL-addressable; transactional pages start at a stable entry URL and the rest of the flow is in-page. Backend search (`https://www.irs.gov/site-index-search?search={term}`) works but the result rankings are uneven; prefer direct URLs when the destination is known.

**Locale.** All shortcuts assume English (`en`). The IRS site provides Spanish (`/es`), Chinese Traditional (`/zh-hant`), Chinese Simplified (`/zh-hans`), Korean (`/ko`), Russian (`/ru`), Vietnamese (`/vi`), and Haitian Creole (`/ht`) translations via top-bar language selector. Locale variants are out of scope for this v0 seed.

Because IRS.gov is a website hosted in Chrome, the per-shortcut interaction model is browser-driven: focus the address bar with `cmd+L`, type the destination URL, press enter. Form fills use `tab` to advance fields and `type_text` for values. Submit buttons activate with enter or by clicking. Verification is almost always `interpret_check` (the agent looks at the rendered page and judges yes/no).
